label: FIXABLE
summary: 1. [FIXABLE] HIGH: Real email addresses that appear inside filenames are now silently not redacted (PII leak). File: lib/redact-patterns.ts, looksLikeAtFilename, wired into the pii.email validator. How it happens: in the pii.email regex `\b([A-Za-z0-9._%+\-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})\b`, the domain class includes dots. So for `jane.doe@gmail.com.json` the span is the whole string and the "domain" is `gmail.com.json`. That domain ends in `.json`, NON_TLD_EXTENSION matches, the validator returns false, and the engine (lib/redact-engine.ts:421) `continue`s. The pattern regex is global, so lastIndex has already moved past the whole span, and the embedded address is never matched again. I checked this by running the shipped PATTERNS/validator under bun. Each of these spans was rejected (validate returned false), so none would be redacted: - `legacy_credentials/jane.doe@gmail.com.json` - `users/alice@acme.io.log` - `deploy@my-proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com.json` - `bob@corp.co.uk.txt` A plain `alice@acme.com` still validates as true. Why it matters in production: per-user files named by email address are common. Examples include gcloud credential paths, service-account key files named `<sa>@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com.json`, per-user export, cache and log files, and `*.csv` dumps named after a mailbox. They show up in stack traces, `ls` output and CI logs, which are exactly what gstack-post.ts publishes after redaction. pii.email is autoRedactable, so this is a straight false negative on outbound text. Fix: strip the matched extension, then exempt only when the remainder is not itself domain-shaped. `2.0`, `4.17.21` and `next` would stay exempt, while `gmail.com` and `acme.io` would still report. For example: - match `const ext = NON_TLD_EXTENSION.exec(domain)` - when it matches, return `!/\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$/.test(domain.slice(0, ext.index))` Add negative tests for `<addr>@<real-domain>.<tld>.json`, `.log` and `.txt`.

summary: 2. [INVESTIGATE] LOW: The version-domain branch of looksLikeAtFilename exempts real addresses at all-numeric hosts. File: lib/redact-patterns.ts, `/^\d+(?:\.\d+)+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$/`. Any address whose host is two or more all-digit labels followed by one alpha label (for example `x@1.2.de`, checked under bun) is now treated as a filename with no extension check at all. Real hostnames of that shape are rare, but they exist (numeric subdomains on short ccTLDs). This branch exists only to catch `pkg@1.2.3.<something>` names that don't already end in a NON_TLD extension, so consider whether it's needed at all.

summary: 3. [INVESTIGATE] LOW: Exempt constants collide with dialable numbers. File: lib/redact-patterns.ts, NUMERIC_CONSTANTS. Examples: - 2^33 = `8589934592` reads as (858) 993-4592, a San Diego format. - 2^31-1 = `2147483647` reads as (214) 748-3647, Dallas. - 2^34 = `17179869184` reads as +1 717-986-9184. The exemption is exact-match and separator-free only, so this is about 51 specific values. It's a theoretical leak, but it's a fixed list that a real person's number can land on, and nothing records that tradeoff.

label: Medium
summary: 1. Medium — Numeric DNS labels bypass email redaction (lib/redact-patterns.ts:492–494). The dotted-version alternative suppresses every address whose domain has two or more numeric labels followed by any alphabetic TLD, including `alice@1.2.com`. Numeric DNS labels are valid: an owner of `2.com` can configure `1.2.com` for mail. No filename, package, or path context is required, so genuine contact records disappear from the PII findings and automatic redaction. Reproduced with the actual scan API: `Customer email: alice@1.2.com` and `Customer email: alice@1.2.org` both return no findings, while `Customer email: alice@2.com` reports `pii.email`. Remove the blanket numeric-domain exemption or require independent filename context before suppressing an address at a real TLD.

label: Medium
summary: 2. Medium — Constant allowlist silently exempts phone numbers even in explicit contact fields (lib/redact-patterns.ts:1028). A phone number does not need a leading plus or punctuation, and several listed constants also have valid national phone-number shapes. The unconditional value exemption drops `Customer phone: 2166136261`, `Customer phone: 2246822507`, and `Customer phone: 2147483647`; all return no findings through the actual scan API. The equivalent `Customer phone: 216-613-6261` and `Customer phone: +12166136261` still report `pii.phone.e164`. A normal digits-only contact export can therefore leak PII solely because its value happens to equal a hash constant or integer limit. Require evidence of a numeric constant's code context instead of globally allowlisting its digits, and preserve detection in phone/contact fields.

label: FIXABLE
summary: pii.email now drops real addresses that appear inside filenames. Location: lib/redact-patterns.ts:492-495 (looksLikeAtFilename), wired in at :1006. The email regex's domain group is greedy (`[A-Za-z0-9.\-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}`), so a filename that embeds an address matches as one span that includes the extension. The NON_TLD_EXTENSION test then exempts that whole span. Exporters, key stores and per-user reports often name files after a person's address, for example `jane.doe@acme.com.csv`, `alice@corp.com.json` or `bob@gmail.com.txt`. I ran the pattern and helper under bun, and each of those spans returned looksLikeAtFilename === true, so no finding is raised. The engine does not re-scan inside a span that fails validation: `continue` resumes at re.lastIndex, past the whole match. That means the embedded `jane.doe@acme.com` is never reported, and an auto-redactable MEDIUM PII leak passes silently. Before this commit, the same span was flagged and redacted. Fix: strip the extension and exempt only when what remains in front of it cannot be an email domain. That means a single dotless label (`next.yaml`), or a dotted all-numeric version (`4.17.21.tgz`, `2.0.json`). For example, `const m = domain.match(/^(.*)\.([A-Za-z]+)$/)`, then require `NON_TLD_EXTENSION.test(domain) && /^(?:[A-Za-z0-9-]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)+)$/.test(m[1])`. Add negative regressions for `<addr>@<domain>.<tld>.csv|json|txt`.

Location: lib/redact-patterns.ts:494, the second regex `/^\d+(?:\.\d+)+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}$/`. Any domain with two or more numeric labels before a genuine TLD is exempt. summary: NUMERIC_CONSTANTS exempts 13 values that are valid-shaped NANP phone numbers, with no context check. Location: lib/redact-patterns.ts:214-231, used at :1028. These are 2147483647/8, 4294967295/6, 4294967291, 8589934591/2, 2654435761, 2654435769, 2166136261, 3432918353, 2246822507 and 3266489909. Each has a valid area code and a valid exchange (214 Dallas, 858 San Diego, 429, 265, 216 Cleveland, 343, 224, 326). The exemption applies even next to `phone:` or `tel:`. Only the separator-free 10-digit form is exempt, and the set is small, so exposure is a handful of specific numbers. Whoever holds such a number would have it pass unredacted, which is theoretical but possible. If that matters, skip the exemption when a phone keyword sits within a short window before the span, the same way isNumericMetadataValue already keeps `"phone":` values reportable.

summary: The NON_TLD_EXTENSION list depends on a dated IANA snapshot, and nothing re-checks it. Location: lib/redact-patterns.ts:478-481. The comment says the list was "checked against the IANA root zone list, 2026-10-28". If a new gTLD that matches one of these extensions is delegated later (`.json`, `.log`, `.lock`, `.conf` and so on), real addresses at that TLD will be silently exempt, and no test will notice. I could not check the current root zone offline. Consider a guard test that pins the list against a vendored TLD list, or a comment naming the re-check owner.

label: Medium
summary: Numeric subdomains bypass email redaction (`lib/redact-patterns.ts:492-494`). The dotted-version alternative accepts any alphabetic final label, including real public TLDs. `alice@10.20.com` is a valid mailbox form: numeric DNS labels are allowed, and an owner of a numeric domain can configure numeric subdomains and MX records. It is not evidence of a filename. At this head, scanning `Contact: alice@10.20.com` yields no findings and `applyRedactions` leaves the address unchanged; the base email pattern accepts it. This silently removes the PII warning and redaction for an entire class of valid addresses. Restrict filename suppression to non-TLD extensions or require independent filename context rather than treating numeric labels under `.com` as proof of a package version.

label: Medium
summary: The constant allowlist suppresses explicitly labeled phone numbers (`lib/redact-patterns.ts:1028`). The new exclusion checks only the digits, without examining whether the surrounding text actually denotes a programming constant. Several listed values also have valid national-phone shapes, including `2147483647` (214-748-3647). Scanning `Phone: 2147483647` now yields no findings, and `applyRedactions` leaves it unchanged; the base phone validator accepts it, and the head still reports the hyphenated spelling. Plain digit-only telephone fields in contact exports and logs therefore lose their warning and redaction merely because their value coincides with an integer constant. Require code/constant context for this exemption, and preserve findings in explicit phone/contact fields.
